correctness.rationale: By group order 2p, subgroups have orders 1,2,p,2p; their left cosets give 2p singletons, p² bipartite pairs, two parts and universe. All two-point supports are realized tracewise. A triple is shattered iff distributed 2+1 between the halves; full, double, singleton, and empty witnesses are explicit. Monochromatic triples fail a two-point trace. Every four-support contains a monochromatic triple or is 2+2, where a 3-point mixed trace cannot be realized. Counts yield 1+2pz+C(2p,2)z²+\(p^2(p-1)\)z³. Independent finite enumeration passed p=3,5,7,11; no infinite claim is based on testing.

value.rationale: All subgroup cosets of a finite group form a canonical incidence family. This provides the exact full shattered-support polynomial for the smallest infinite nonabelian family, giving a qualitative structural contrast with cyclic coset systems of the same order: the reflection-coset pairs create precisely the mixed three-point supports and increase VC dimension from two to three. The full support census is a natural complete invariant beyond a scalar bound; it is not claimed as a broad arbitrary-group theorem. The proof is short but not merely substituting parameters into an earlier formula.
